toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Collected two items. X8 (maintenance export) first, to cross-tab the 11 complaint vans against workshop, pads, Upper Wend exposure and drivers. Then X13 (Northfield's own records), which X8 pointed to, to find what was different about the work done there. I skipped the other items because they could not change the answers.
output.brief:
The evidence points away from driver technique. The soft pedals come from water-contaminated brake fluid.

While our brake bay was closed, Northfield Motor Services changed the fluid in 13 Eastgate vans. Eleven were filled from a bulk drum opened in March, its cap found missing in August. Those eleven are exactly the eleven complaint vans, including LK-209; the two filled from a fresh drum have no complaints. Northfield tested two complaint vans: fluid boiled near 150°C versus 255°C for sealed stock. Renewing it, pads untouched, ended the complaints on those two. The same drivers in other vans on the same hills report nothing, and the other 25 Eastgate vans, 23 on the same pads, are fine. Northfield warned us on 25 September to recheck the rest; no reply is on file.

I'm about 90% sure. This week: pull all 13 Northfield vans, test the fluid, renew it from sealed stock, then return them. Don't discipline or retrain drivers; they reported a real fault. Hold the pad-supplier switch; the squeal link is unproven. Then find out why the warning went unanswered.
